ufbx_write — vendored source
=============================

Upstream:  https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx-write
Commit:    2b65caaaa7fada7db9a2d25cd924997838169056
License:   MIT OR Unlicense — see LICENSE

What is vendored
----------------
`ufbx_write.h` and `ufbx_write.c` from the commit above, **plus this
project's patches**, recorded as `review.patch` (a unified diff against the
pristine upstream files). Refreshing this directory is therefore: copy the
newer upstream pair in, update the hash above, re-apply `review.patch`
(`git apply third_party/ufbx-write/review.patch`, resolving any drift by
hand), regenerate the patch from the result (`git diff -- ufbx_write.h
ufbx_write.c > review.patch` before committing), then re-run the workspace
tests — `crates/optimize`'s `ufbxw_patches` suite exercises every hunk, and
its export round-trips re-import written files through the vendored ufbx
reader. Drop a hunk only once upstream provides the same thing.

The patches (each hunk is marked `review patch P<n>` in the source)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The exporter retains every source property the optimization stack did not
change, and four things it needs to write had no upstream entry point:

P1  Property flags and value kinds. `ufbxw_set_prop_flags()` /
    `ufbxw_get_prop_flags()` set `UFBXW_PROP_FLAG_USER` / `_ANIMATABLE` /
    `_HIDDEN` (new) on an existing property, and the `Properties70` writer
    emits them as the SDK does (`"A+U"`, `"U"`, `"H"`) where it previously
    wrote only `A`. `UFBXW_PROP_FLAG_EXPLICIT` (never written to the file)
    makes the writer emit a property even when its value equals the template
    default it would otherwise elide it for, so a source's explicit properties
    reach the output verbatim. `ufbxw_add_real_string()` adds a
    `Distance`-typed value, `ufbxw_add_blob()` a `Blob` (upstream asserted on
    writing one); the ASCII writer gains the `R` (raw bytes) format the binary
    writer already had.

P2  `Null` node attribute. `ufbxw_create_null()` attaches a `Null` attribute
    (template `FbxNull`: `Color`, `Size`, `Look`) so an empty / locator round
    trips as one instead of an attribute-less Model. The element writer emits
    its `TypeFlags: "Null"`, and — the same site — the `TypeFlags: "Camera"`
    + `GeometryVersion` cameras were written without.

P3  Topology layers. Five `ufbxw_mesh_attribute` kinds for the generic
    `ufbxw_mesh_set_attribute()`: `EDGE_CREASE` (`LayerElementEdgeCrease`,
    real, ByEdge), `VERTEX_CREASE` (`LayerElementVertexCrease`, real,
    ByVertice), `HOLE` (`LayerElementHole`, ByPolygon), `VISIBILITY`
    (`LayerElementVisibility`, ByEdge), `POLYGON_GROUP`
    (`LayerElementPolygonGroup`, int, ByPolygon). Hole and Visibility are
    written as 0/1 int arrays, exactly as upstream writes `Smoothing`.

P4  LOD groups and layered textures. `ufbxw_create_lod_group()` +
    `ufbxw_lod_group_add_level()` write a `LodGroup` node attribute (template
    `FbxLODGroup`) with the per-level `Thresholds|Level<n>` (Distance) and
    `DisplayLevels|Level<n>` (enum) properties ufbx derives its levels from.
    `UFBXW_TEXTURE_LAYERED` + `ufbxw_texture_add_layer()` write a
    `LayeredTexture` object (its own object type and `FbxLayeredTexture`
    template) with `BlendModes` / `Alphas` arrays parallel to the layer
    connections, which go out as plain OO connections from each layer.

P5  Curve nodes without curves. `ufbxw_animate_prop_masked()` (and `_len`)
    take a component bit mask and create an `AnimationCurve` only for the
    components in it; the `d|X`/`d|Y`/`d|Z` default properties are always
    present. Upstream's `ufbxw_animate_prop()` creates one curve per
    component and offers no way to remove one (`ufbxw_delete_element()`
    leaves the curve node's connection list pointing at the freed slot).
    Maya writes curve nodes that carry only their defaults — every bone's
    `Lcl Scaling`, its `lockInfluenceWeights` — and a reader treats any
    curve, even an empty one, as a non-constant value: ufbx then adds a
    scale helper under each such node, so a re-read of the export had 42
    nodes the source did not.

Everything else is upstream's, untouched: the patches add table rows,
element types, tokens and entry points beside the existing ones and change
four writer sites (property flags, blob values, the node-attribute /
texture bodies, the curve-node builder).

Stability
---------
Upstream states plainly that ufbx_write "is still a work-in-progress, and
issues/breaking changes are to be expected". That is why the commit is pinned
rather than tracking a branch, and why the export round-trip test exists: a
breaking change upstream should fail a test here rather than silently produce
files that no longer load.

How it is built
---------------
`crates/optimize/build.rs` compiles this alongside `src/export_bridge.c` with
`cc`, and sets `cfg(has_ufbxw)` only when this directory is present — the same
optional-vendoring contract `crates/import` has for ufbx. Delete this directory
and the workspace still builds; export then reports `OptError::Unavailable`.
In non-release profiles it also compiles `src/ufbxw_probe.c`
(`cfg(has_ufbxw_probe)`), the test-only scene that drives every patched entry
point for `tests/ufbxw_patches.rs`.

`ufbx_write.c` needs C99 or later. It has no OS-specific code and no threading
unless explicitly opted in, so nothing extra is configured. Note the header
defines `ufbxw_real` as `double`, so every coordinate crossing the bridge is
`f64` — `crates/optimize/src/export.rs` converts on the way in.
